info.title: APEX API
info.description:
Stock analysis: technical indicators, opportunity scoring, strategy backtesting and walk-forward-validated price-direction forecasting.

**This API never places trades.** It is an analysis tool, and nothing it returns is financial advice.

post.description:
Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token, rotating the
refresh token. Replaying an already-used token revokes the whole
family and forces a fresh sign-in.
Revoke every session for this account — the 'sign out everywhere' action.

get.description: Search by ticker or company name — 'apple' and 'AAPL' both find AAPL.

Technical analysis: latest indicator values, the signal summary, and
suggested exit levels. Mirrors the Analysis tab.
Opportunity score with entry/target/stop — one dashboard card.

ML price-direction forecast.

`has_skill` is computed here rather than left to the client: a model
that loses to its majority-class baseline has no demonstrated skill, and
presenting the direction without that flag invites misreading.

TradingView technical rating. Returns null rather than erroring when the
unofficial upstream is unavailable — it is display-only.

get.description: Holdings priced at the latest quote, with totals.

Win rate computed from the user's own logged trades. Returns null rather
than a placeholder when nothing is logged — a hardcoded '68%' shown to
every user is the bug this replaced.

post.description: Backtest the momentum strategy over two years of daily bars.

post.summary: Run a scan (synchronous — moves to /jobs in Phase 4)
post.description:
Synchronous scan.

Measured: ~21s for the personal universe, ~46s broad. That exceeds
Vercel's serverless cap and typical nginx/ALB 60s defaults, so clients
should not rely on this endpoint. Marked deprecated from the day it
ships; Phase 4 replaces it with POST /jobs/scan returning a job id.

Assistant reply. The user's own holdings are passed in as context —
never imported from module state, so one account's positions cannot
appear in another's conversation.

Start a market scan and return immediately.

Measured: ~21s for the personal universe, ~46s broad. Both are past
what an HTTP request should hold open, so this never runs inline.
Poll GET /jobs/{id} for progress.

get.description:
Poll a job. 404 covers both 'no such job' and 'not yours', so the
endpoint cannot be used to discover that another account's job exists.

delete.description:
Request cancellation. A running scan stops at the next symbol
boundary — the work in between is a blocking network call.

post.description:
Receive a TradingView alert.

TradingView sends the alert message body verbatim: JSON if the alert was
written as JSON, otherwise plain text. Both are accepted.

get.description:
Liveness plus the auth configuration, so a deployment serving cookies
without Secure, or running on a generated dev key, is visible rather
than silently insecure.

SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse
SessionResponse.description:
Returned on register / login / refresh.

Browsers should use the httpOnly cookies set alongside this and echo
`csrf_token` in the X-CSRF-Token header on state-changing requests.
`access_token` is included for non-browser clients only.
